explanation_es:
Los verbos modales son auxiliares que acompañan a otro verbo para expresar habilidad, permiso, posibilidad, obligación, prohibición, consejo o cortesía. Los principales son can, could, must, should, may, might y would. Have to no es un modal puro, pero se estudia con ellos porque también expresa obligación.

La forma es siempre igual: modal más verbo en forma base, sin to y sin -s en tercera persona. Se dice She can code, nunca She cans code ni She can to code. La excepción es have to, que sí lleva to y sí cambia: he has to, I had to. Para negar se agrega not: can't (cannot, en una sola palabra), couldn't, mustn't, shouldn't. Para preguntar se invierten modal y sujeto: Can you work on weekends? Con have to se usa do: Do you have to wear a uniform?

Can es habilidad o permiso en presente; could es habilidad en pasado o petición cortés; must es obligación fuerte, típica de normas escritas o de lo que el hablante considera necesario; have to es obligación que viene de afuera, como una regla; should es consejo; may y might son posibilidad, y may también es permiso formal; would es cortesía o situación hipotética. Must no tiene pasado: para obligaciones pasadas se usa had to.

La confusión clave para hispanohablantes está en las negaciones. No tengo que se dice don't have to y significa que no es necesario. No debes, en el sentido de está prohibido, se dice mustn't. Son ideas opuestas: You don't have to come on Saturday da libertad; You mustn't share the password prohíbe.

En el examen escrito, busca estas señales: rule, law, necessary llevan a must o have to; advice, good idea a should; not necessary a don't have to; forbidden, prohibited a mustn't; maybe, perhaps a may o might; polite request a could o would; ability, able to a can o could.

contrast.en: I can write code in Python.
contrast.note_es: Can va seguido del verbo en forma base. En español el segundo verbo va en infinitivo (escribir), pero en inglés no se agrega to ni ninguna terminación.

contrast.en: You must back up the database before you deploy the app.
contrast.es: Tienes que hacer una copia de seguridad de la base de datos antes de desplegar la aplicación.
contrast.note_es: Must expresa obligación fuerte y nunca cambia: he must, she must, sin -s y sin to. En español se dice tienes que o debes.

contrast.en: You mustn't share your password with anyone.
contrast.es: No debes compartir tu contraseña con nadie.
contrast.note_es: Mustn't es prohibición: está prohibido hacerlo. No significa no tienes que; eso sería don't have to.

contrast.en: I don't have to work on Sundays.
contrast.es: No tengo que trabajar los domingos.
contrast.note_es: Don't have to significa que no es necesario: puedo hacerlo o no. Es lo opuesto a mustn't, aunque en español ambas frases empiezan con no.

contrast.en: You should test the code before you send it.
contrast.es: Deberías probar el código antes de enviarlo.
contrast.note_es: Should es consejo o recomendación y equivale a deberías. Suena más suave que must.

contrast.en: Could you send me the report, please?
contrast.es: ¿Me podría enviar el informe, por favor?
contrast.note_es: Could sirve para pedir algo con cortesía, no solo para hablar del pasado. Lo natural es responder Sure o Of course; no se responde Yes, I could.

contrast.es: Puede que el servidor esté caído.
contrast.note_es: Might y may expresan posibilidad, no certeza. En español decimos puede que o de pronto; en inglés basta con poner might antes del verbo en forma base: might be, no might is.

common_errors.why_es: Los modales no llevan to. El error viene de traducir puedo usar pensando en el infinitivo español. Solo have to lleva to.
Después de un modal el verbo va en forma base. Ni el modal ni el verbo que lo sigue llevan -s en tercera persona.

common_errors.wrong: You mustn't come on Saturday. It's optional.
common_errors.right: You don't have to come on Saturday. It's optional.
common_errors.why_es: Mustn't es prohibición. Si la idea es que no es necesario, se usa don't have to. En español ambas ideas se dicen con no, por eso se confunden.

common_errors.wrong: Do you can work on weekends?
common_errors.why_es: La pregunta con modal se forma invirtiendo el modal y el sujeto, sin do. Solo have to usa do: Do you have to work on weekends?

common_errors.wrong: I will can finish the project next week.
common_errors.right: I will be able to finish the project next week.
common_errors.why_es: En español decimos podré, pero en inglés no se pueden juntar dos modales como will y can. Para el futuro de can se usa will be able to.

common_errors.wrong: I have to go to work yesterday.
common_errors.right: I had to go to work yesterday.
common_errors.why_es: Have to sí cambia de tiempo: en pasado es had to. Must no tiene forma de pasado, así que para obligaciones pasadas se usa had to.

common_errors.right: I don't have to work late.
common_errors.why_es: Must no se niega con don't. Su negación es mustn't, que significa prohibido. Si la idea es que no es necesario, la forma correcta es don't have to.

oral_questions.question: What do you have to do before you deploy an application?
oral_questions.model_answer: I have to test the code first. I must also back up the database.
oral_questions.focus: have to y must para obligación, seguidos de verbo en forma base

oral_questions.question: What should a new employee do on the first day?
oral_questions.model_answer: I think a new employee should arrive early. He or she should ask questions when something isn't clear.
oral_questions.focus: should para consejo, sin -s en tercera persona

oral_questions.question: Can you work on weekends?
oral_questions.model_answer: Yes, I can work on Saturdays. But I can't work on Sundays because I study at SENA.
oral_questions.focus: can y can't para disponibilidad, respuesta corta más explicación

oral_questions.question: What mustn't you do with company data?
oral_questions.model_answer: I mustn't share company data with people outside the company. I mustn't copy it to my personal USB drive either.

oral_questions.question: Do you have to wear a uniform at SENA?
oral_questions.model_answer: No, I don't have to wear a uniform. But I have to bring my ID card to enter.
oral_questions.focus: have to y don't have to para obligación externa y ausencia de necesidad, pregunta con do

oral_questions.question: What couldn't you do last year that you can do now?
oral_questions.model_answer: Last year I couldn't create a database. Now I can design tables and write SQL queries.
oral_questions.focus: couldn't para habilidad pasada frente a can para habilidad presente

oral_questions.question: How would you ask your boss for a day off?
oral_questions.model_answer: I would say: Could I have Friday off, please? I have an exam at SENA.
oral_questions.focus: would para situación hipotética y could para petición cortés

oral_questions.question: Why might a user have problems with your access-control system?
oral_questions.model_answer: The user might have a damaged ID card. Also, the system may be offline because of a network problem.

oral_questions.question: What do the workers have to do in your project when equipment leaves the building?
oral_questions.model_answer: In my project, they have to register the equipment in the system. They also have to write the name of the person who takes it.
oral_questions.focus: have to para describir las reglas de un proceso laboral

oral_questions.question: Should companies let employees use their phones at work?
oral_questions.model_answer: I think they should, but with limits. Employees shouldn't use their phones in important meetings.
oral_questions.focus: should y shouldn't para dar una opinión

roleplay.situation_es: Es tu primer día como desarrollador junior en una empresa de software. Tu jefa te explica las reglas del equipo y tú haces preguntas con cortesía sobre horarios, equipos y acceso a la base de datos. Practica have to, don't have to, must, mustn't, can, can't, could, should, would y might.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.line: Welcome to the team. First, you have to sign in with your ID card every morning.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Okay. Do I have to arrive at a specific time?

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.line: You should arrive before nine, but you don't have to stay after six.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Good. Can I use my own laptop for work?

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.line: No, sorry. You must use the company computer, and you mustn't copy company data to personal devices.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: I understand. Could you give me access to the database, please?

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.line: Sure, but this week you can only read it. You can't change anything yet.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: That's fine. Should I ask someone before I upload my code?

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.line: Yes. You must ask a senior developer to review your code first.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Perfect. One more question: would it be possible to work from home on Fridays?

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.line: It might be possible after your first month. We can talk about it later.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Thank you. I think I should start reading the project documentation now.
